A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAVFlow and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison. The complete documents were inspected, including v2's new Appendices A–D; v1 ends with references and has no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original translation, speaker-similarity, emotion, visual-quality and human MOS results, alongside a modality-guidance ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds emotion fine-tuning results, class-wise analyses, qualitative examples and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The unit translator, duration predictor, dual guidance, OT-CFM objectives, vocoder and face renderer remain the same. Section 4.1 makes source-duration matching explicit where v1 already described target-length interpolation, without establishing a new algorithm. EmoFAN remains the guidance encoder; MAE-DFER replaces an evaluation model.

E1.justification: The same MuAViC/LRS3 translation and reconstruction coverage, five languages, and CREMA-D emotion domain remain. Additional CREMA-D fine-tuning changes the training condition within existing coverage. The corrected six-emotion description and changed classifier do not establish a new evaluated population or task.

E2.justification: v2 Table 10 adds ASR+YourTTS+TFG and ASR+XTTS+TFG to the visual-emotion comparison, whereas v1 Table 6 compared only ground truth, AV2AV and MAVFlow. These cascaded methods already appeared in audio comparisons. The principal translation and MOS comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Visual-emotion evaluation changes from five-class EmoFAN to six-class MAE-DFER, with ES and UAR/WAR metrics added. v2 also introduces CREMA-D fine-tuning and a full-pipeline timing comparison using one A6000 and a 2.35-second input. The stated training source for retained Table 2 results changes from LRS3-only in v1 Section 5.4 to MuAViC in v2 Section 5.6, without establishing that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained guidance ablation, v2 tests the effect of emotion-dataset fine-tuning and adds class-wise audio/visual diagnostics, temporal emotion-transition examples and an inference-speed comparison. Section 5.6 and Appendices A–C substantially expand analysis beyond v1's modality ablation and single anger example. v1 Table 7 is retained as v2 Table 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated training seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates for the experimental scores. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 6 replaces GT/AV2AV/MAVFlow visual-emotion accuracies of 31.95/30.61/33.29 with 76.83/67.20/72.68 under the changed evaluator; these are not same-setting gains. New results include MAVFlow+ audio accuracy of 51.46%, versus 36.46% without additional training, ES scores, class-wise findings and timings of 1.66/1.22/1.75 seconds for MAVFlow/AV2AV/four-stage cascade. Tables 1–5 and the renumbered guidance ablation retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same flow formulation, objectives and embedding definitions. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. The added standard evaluation-metric descriptions do not introduce new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same core contribution: dual-guided CFM for zero-shot AV2AV translation preserving speaker identity and emotion. The headline 36% speaker-consistency claim and lip-sync/FID improvements remain unchanged. Naming LSE/FID in the abstract clarifies existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation through class-specific strengths and weaknesses, the benefits of emotion-rich training, and explanations of temporal emotion preservation. Appendix D newly identifies missing explicit audio-emotion guidance and reliance on inherited semantic translation modules as limitations. Meanwhile, v1's specific LRS3-to-CREMA-D domain-shift caveat is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access statement and specifies the hardware, input duration and pipeline scope of its timing measurement. Section 4.1 documents source-duration matching while omitting v1's batch-padding and separate modality-interpolation details. Main hardware, learning-rate and embedding-size disclosures remain; the added fine-tuning lacks a specified budget or split.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to CosyVoice and MAE-DFER. Section 4.1 explicitly credits AV2AV's duration-prediction structure and distinguishes source-duration preservation for dubbing. The broader related-work narrative and positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, rewrites the duration-regulator explanation, creates a dedicated Section 5.6 for ablations, and adds acknowledgements and organized appendices. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact rather than undergoing extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the overview in Figure 1, refreshes Figure 2, and reformats Figure 3 with frame indices and revised annotations. It expands Table 6 with ES, adds Tables 7, 9 and 10 plus Figure 4, and reformats or relocates retained tables with revised emphasis and spacing. These constitute substantial changes to the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves evaluation quality by replacing the mismatched five-class visual evaluator with one covering the six stated CREMA-D emotions, and adds useful class-wise failures, runtime evidence, limitations and code-access information. The gains are qualified by sparse fine-tuning details and the unexplained LRS3-to-MuAViC training-description change for retained results. Overall, these provide a clear but limited improvement in validation and transparency.
